author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
title: The Complete Poetical Works of Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
edition: Household Edition, Houghton Mifflin Company; publisher note dated Boston, Autumn 1902. Original English poems only; PG plain-text spelling, punctuation, line breaks and indentation retained; blank space outside stanzas trimmed. The library text holds the whole Gutenberg volume from Voices of the Night to the end of the translations (original poems, dramas, translations and Longfellow’s own notes); only the quoted publisher’s note, the contents and the separators between books are left out. Verse keeps its transcription lines and indentation; wrapped prose notes and stage directions are joined as paragraphs. The PG text of nineteen poems (Woods in Winter, The Skeleton in Armor, The Wreck of the Hesperus, Excelsior, Rain in Summer, The Secret of the Sea, Sir Humphrey Gilbert, The Lighthouse, The Phantom Ship, The Emperor’s Bird’s-Nest, The Ropewalk, Paul Revere’s Ride, The Birds of Killingworth, The Bell of Atri, Christmas Bells, The Sermon of St. Francis, The Leap of Roushan Beg, From My Arm-Chair and The Tide Rises, the Tide Falls) was later collated word by word against the OCR of the Internet Archive scan of this edition (complongworks00fellrich), every difference decided on its page images: 69 readings were corrected to the print, most of them scanning errors (“month” for “mouth,” “Squirt” for “Squire,” “Syndie” for “Syndic,” “Bat” for “But,” “Death I” for “‘Death!’,” “But the sea in the darkness calls and calls” for “But the sea, the sea in the darkness calls”) and lost or altered punctuation, and the indentation of four stanzas was set as printed; the stop after “scene” in Woods in Winter, a period or a broken comma, is left as a comma. The Old Clock on the Stairs and The Three Kings were later collated the same way and corrected to the print in these places: the accents and punctuation of the French epigraph (“L’éternité est une pendule dont”; “tombeaux; ‘Toujours, jamais! Jamais, toujours!’”), “miser” for “Miser,” a comma for the full stop after “throbs of pain,” “saddlebows” for “saddle-bows” (printed “sad-dlebows,” broken inside the word), “inn yard” for “inn-yard,” and two lost commas, a lost semicolon and a lost dash in The Three Kings; the epigraph’s attribution keeps the transcription’s “--JACQUES BRIDAINE.”

rights.basis: The selected original English text was published in 1902, before 1931, and its US copyright term has expired as of 2026. Project Gutenberg explicitly lists this ebook as Public domain in the USA. No modern editorial front matter, illustrations or translations are reproduced.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg plain text (eBook 1365, UTF-8, CRLF normalised to LF) from the PG mirror. Kept everything from VOICES OF THE NIGHT to the last translation; removed the PG header and footer, the quoted publisher’s note and the contents, the transcriber’s angle-bracketed pointers to the Hiawatha notes, and the row-of-asterisks separators between books. Each blank-line separated chunk became a block: a single capitalised line is a heading (level 1 after a separator, otherwise level 2); verse chunks are stanzas with the transcription’s lines and indentation kept and only trailing spaces removed; chunks of wrapped prose (Longfellow’s prefatory notes, his Hiawatha notes, and stage directions) were detected by long lines whose continuations start in lower case and joined into paragraphs, keeping spacing inside lines. Converted by a scratch Node script; every nightly reading was located exactly.
